# Flow Messaging

> Flow Messaging is a two-way messaging API for AI agents on Telegram, iMessage and WhatsApp. Flow hosts the senders (bots, lines, numbers), delivers every inbound message to your webhook or WebSocket as a signed, ordered event, and passes every send through one gate that enforces each channel's rules. Base URL: https://api.flow.engineer. Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` (`fk_test_...` for the sandbox, `fk_live_...` for your own senders).

**No key? `curl -X POST https://api.flow.engineer/v1/sandbox/keys`**: no account, no API key sent. Save `key` as `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` and `claim_token` as `FLOW_CLAIM_TOKEN` (both shown once; e.g. in `.env`, gitignored), then show the person a sender's `address.link` and `join_code` from the answer. Check `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` first: never get a new key when you already have one.

Key facts for coding agents:

- Keys: `POST /v1/sandbox/keys` (no account) answers `201` with `key` (`fk_test_...`), `claim_token` (`fct_...`), `claim_url` (holds the token; treat it like one), `app` (with `sandbox_join_code`), `api_key.expires_at`, `allowance` and `senders` (the shared sandbox senders, each with `address.link` and `join_code`). Rate limited per client address (`429 rate_limited`, `retry_after`). The CLI does the same: `npx @flow-engineer/messaging init` (writes both to `.env`, prints the sandbox link and join code). Read the key from `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY`; the webhook secret from `FLOW_MESSAGING_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- Sandbox allowance: without an account, 1 contact and 50 messages in total on the Telegram sandbox (WhatsApp's when it opens), and the key expires after 7 days (then it stops working and the contact is removed; a person can still claim the app). Signed in: 3 contacts x 100 messages each, no expiry, one allowance per person shared by every app they own or claim (up to 10 claimed apps). iMessage is in neither. Only outbound messages count; simulated conversations (below) are free and take no contact slot, so never make a second app to test. `GET /v1/app` returns `allowance` (`tier`, `channels`, `contacts`, `messages_per_contact`, `messages` {`limit`, `used`, `remaining`}, `expires_at`, `upgrade`).
- Sign in to keep the app (GitHub): `npx @flow-engineer/messaging login` (uses `FLOW_CLAIM_TOKEN`, replaces `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` in `.env`; `--no-wait` for agents that cannot block, then run `login` again after approval). Or `POST /v1/device/authorizations {"claim_token":"fct_...","client_name":"Claude Code"}`, show the person `verification_uri` and `user_code` (never `device_code`): they open the page, sign in and type the code you show them (a link alone never approves), then poll `POST /v1/device/token {"device_code":"fdc_..."}` every `interval` seconds (`429` = slow down) until `approved` (new `key`: replace `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` with it, since the old sandbox key stops working once the new one is handed out; drop `FLOW_CLAIM_TOKEN`), `denied` or `expired` (start again). The app and its data are kept. A claim through `claim_url` in a browser gives no new key and revokes the sandbox key, unless the person ticks "Keep my agent's current key working" (then it works without expiry; an expired one works again if claimed within 30 days). After a claim that revoked it, ask the person for a key from the dashboard's Keys page, or sign in with the device flow above.
- Allowance errors: `403 permission` with `channel_code` `sandbox_allowance_used`, `sandbox_contact_limit`, `sandbox_channel_not_included` or `sign_in_required`; an expired sandbox key is `401 authentication`, `sandbox_key_expired`. Fix: have a person sign in (an expired key still claims its app for 30 days), or get a new key.
- Dashboard: https://api.flow.engineer/admin (sign in with GitHub). Signed in, you can make live keys (`fk_live_...`) yourself (switch to Live, then Keys > Create live key: https://api.flow.engineer/admin/keys?mode=live; a sandbox app is claimed first) and go live on Telegram with your own bot; keep the live key in its own variable (for example `FLOW_MESSAGING_LIVE_KEY`) so it does not replace your test key. iMessage lines, SMS numbers and WhatsApp numbers are arranged with the Flow team (samyak@flow.engineer; what to send them, and never secrets: https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#what-the-flow-team-arranges-and-how-to-ask). If the user asks for WhatsApp, tell them WhatsApp numbers are arranged with the Flow team, and build and test on Telegram meanwhile: the code does not change per channel.
- Join the Telegram sandbox: the shared bot is in the key's `senders` (or `GET /v1/senders?channel=telegram`); open its `address.link` (`https://t.me/<bot>?start=<code>`) on a phone and tap Start to join your app (or send its `join_code`, e.g. `join wild-otter-04508705`). Then write to the bot: you get `message.received`.
- Test without a phone (test key only): `POST /v1/test/conversations {"channel":"sms"}` (or `telegram`, `whatsapp`, `imessage`) creates a conversation with a simulated contact; `POST /v1/test/conversations/{conversation_id}/inbound {"content":{"type":"text","text":"hi"}}` writes as that contact (media: upload with `POST /v1/files`, then `{"type":"media","kind":"image","file_id":"file_..."}`). Your agent gets a real `message.received` (webhook, stream, event log, in order; the conversation has `simulated: true`) and replies with its normal send, which passes the real gate and ends `message.sent` without touching a network (on Telegram, as with a real bot, a send before the contact's first turn ends `message.failed`, `channel_code` `403`). `GET /v1/test/conversations/{conversation_id}/transcript` lists both sides oldest first, with `shown` (what the contact saw after fallback). Free: no sandbox contact slot and no messages used, even on an app without an account (its one contact stays free for your phone); tell real from simulated by `simulated: true` on the conversation, the contact and the event's `conversation`. Live keys get `403 permission` (`test_mode_only`). Simulated SMS keeps the contact's rules: a send before the contact's first turn needs `consent` (`403 permission`, `consent_required`), a STOP turn opts the contact out (`opted_out_via` `keyword`; sends answer `contact_opted_out`) until a START turn, with no keyword reply in the transcript; no quiet hours, and media goes as MMS. Simulated WhatsApp keeps WhatsApp's rules: the contact's turns open the 24-hour window, outside it only a `template` goes (`409 outside_window`), and edits and unsends are refused. A HIPAA account can simulate only SMS (`403 permission`, `hipaa_channel_not_covered`).
- Receive events on a webhook (public HTTPS only) or the WebSocket `GET wss://api.flow.engineer/v1/stream` (no public URL; use it for local development). The stream also takes `send` frames. Without `after` the stream starts live (nothing earlier is replayed); with `after=evt_...` it replays from there, then goes live. To run a webhook handler on localhost with no tunnel: `npx @flow-engineer/messaging listen --forward-to http://localhost:3000/webhook` reads the stream and `POST`s each event there, signed like a real delivery with `FLOW_MESSAGING_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- Event log: `GET /v1/events` lists events oldest first. Query parameters: `after` (an event ID: the events after it), `before`, `limit` (1 to 100), `type` (repeat for several: `type=message.received&type=message.failed`), `conversation` (`conv_...`). The answer is `{"data": [...], "has_more": true|false}`; page on with `after` set to the last `id`. Use it to catch up after downtime or when you cannot hold a WebSocket.
- Ask, wait for the reply, continue (CLI, script, test): open the stream first, then find a join that already happened with `GET /v1/conversations?channel=telegram` (newest first; skip `simulated: true`), send, wait for `message.sent`/`message.failed` with that message's `id`, then the next `message.received` in the conversation, with a timeout. TypeScript recipe: https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#14-recipes-common-tasks
- Reply into conversations (`conv_...`) with `POST /v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages`, in the webhook answer as `{"reply": <content>}`, or with a stream `send` frame.
- Verify `Flow-Signature` (`t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "t.{t}.{raw body}">`, keyed with the `whsec_...` secret) before parsing a webhook body; dedupe on `event.id`; answer 2xx within 10 seconds.
- Send, start and edit bodies refuse unknown top-level fields (`400 invalid_request`, `param` names it); there are no scheduled sends (`send_at`).
- Send `Idempotency-Key` on every POST (it makes your retries safe; separately, a send whose outcome the channel left unknown is resent once, so on Telegram a rare duplicate is possible); switch on `error.type`, never on the message text. Read `error.hint` first: it says what to change for this case; `error.doc_url` (`https://api.flow.engineer/docs/errors/<type>`) is the type's page.
- Every send ends `message.sent` or `message.failed`. Telegram never sends `message.delivered` or `message.read`. Text caps: 4096 characters on Telegram (counted in UTF-16 code units, so an emoji such as 😀 is 2), 9999 on iMessage; a media caption takes 1024, also when you edit it.
- Sending limits (dedicated senders): Telegram bots send about 20 messages a second (burst 40; faster is `429 rate_limited`). New conversations per sender: WhatsApp 50 a day and 10 an hour (plus Meta's tier), SMS 1000 and 200, iMessage 4 an hour; past them `429 new_contact_limit`. The sender's `limits` shows its numbers (`messages_per_second`, `new_contacts_per_day`, `new_contacts_per_hour`). The same first message to 20 new contacts within an hour, 80% of 20 or more starts in 72 hours unanswered, or 10 blocks in a day throttle the sender for 24 hours: starts answer `429 sender_throttled` with `retry_after`, replies still go.
- Go live on Telegram: with a live key, `POST /v1/senders {"channel":"telegram","telegram_bot_token":"..."}` connects your own bot (`200`, the sender `active`; connecting the same bot again updates that sender), and `DELETE /v1/senders/{sender_id}` disconnects it. Webhook endpoints and their secrets belong to one mode: register the endpoint again with the live key and store its new secret. `POST /v1/senders` for iMessage, SMS or WhatsApp answers `501 not_implemented` first, with any key (the Flow team connects those): build meanwhile on simulated conversations of that channel. Read the token from an env var; never paste it into a chat or commit it.
- iMessage lines are connected by the Flow team and listed only with a live key. The person always writes first (replies only); get them to write with the line's opt-in link (`address.link` of the sender).
- SMS (US): in pilot. US numbers are connected by the Flow team (live key only, no sandbox). Starts need the contact's recorded `consent` unless they texted first; STOP opts a contact out (`403 permission`, `contact_opted_out`) until START; quiet hours answer `409 outside_window`, `quiet_hours`, with `retry_after`. Text up to 1530 characters and 10 segments.
- Build the app on the REST API (HTTP and the WebSocket stream) for everything it does at runtime: receive, reply, start conversations. In TypeScript or JavaScript use the SDK, `npm install @flow-engineer/messaging` (it also has the CLI: `npx ... init`, `login`); Python and Go SDKs are not published yet, so use HTTP there.
- MCP server (optional, for development): `https://api.flow.engineer/mcp`, with the same key as a Bearer token. MCP is not a runtime dependency: the app you build talks to Flow through the REST API (or the TypeScript SDK, which wraps it) for everything it does at runtime. Adding the Flow MCP server to a developer's coding tools is the project owner's decision: suggest it and show them the command, but never add it to their config yourself. For Claude Code the command is `claude mcp add --transport http flow https://api.flow.engineer/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY"` (Codex and Cursor: section 12 of https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md); `FLOW_MESSAGING_KEY` must be set when it runs (unset, the header is saved as `Bearer ` with no key), and the client loads a new server only after a restart. If its tools are already available to you, use them for sandbox testing; after a test send, wait for `message.sent` or `message.failed`.

## Docs

- [Agent quickstart](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md): everything needed to integrate, with curl, TypeScript and Python: getting a key in one call, the sandbox allowance, signing in to keep the app, the Telegram sandbox, the WebSocket stream, the event log, webhooks and signature checks, `message.received`, replies, your own Telegram bot, idempotency, errors, rate limits, channel notes (Telegram, iMessage, SMS), the optional MCP server, recipes for common tasks.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://api.flow.engineer/openapi.yaml): the full contract (OpenAPI 3.1, version 2026-11-01): every endpoint, schema, event type and error type.
- [Error types](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/errors): one page per `error.type` (what it means, why it happens, how to fix it), the page each error's `doc_url` points at.

## Optional

- [Get a key, allowance, sign in](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#0-get-a-test-key-one-call-no-account): one call without an account; what it allows; the device flow.
- [Telegram sandbox](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#2-join-the-telegram-sandbox-test-key): join from your phone in a minute.
- [Simulated contacts](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#test-without-a-phone-simulated-contacts): test your agent end to end with no phone, on Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage or SMS.
- [Local development](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#3-receive-events-websocket-local-dev-or-webhook): the WebSocket stream, or `listen --forward-to` for a webhook handler on localhost.
- [Sent but not received](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#sent-but-not-received-a-checklist): a checklist from the message's status to the sandbox join.
- [Sending limits](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#sending-limits-and-abuse-signals): pacing, new contacts per day and hour, what throttles a sender.
- [Your own Telegram bot](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#7-go-live-with-your-own-telegram-bot): connect a BotFather token with a live key.
- [Channel notes](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#11-channel-notes): Telegram and iMessage statuses, limits, buttons, reactions, edit and unsend.
- [Errors and retries](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#9-errors-switch-on-errortype): what each `error.type` means and whether to retry.
- [What the Flow team arranges, and how to ask](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#what-the-flow-team-arranges-and-how-to-ask): SMS numbers (also on your own SMS provider account), WhatsApp on your own WhatsApp Business Account, iMessage lines, Python, pricing (billing is not live: free today), support; what to send, never secrets.
- [Recipes for common tasks](https://api.flow.engineer/docs/quickstart.md#14-recipes-common-tasks): ask and wait for a reply; many Telegram bots; serverless webhooks; files and voice notes; WhatsApp reminders; moving a polling bot; broadcasts; deleting a contact (GDPR); a leaked key; prototype to production; one bot per customer; delivery guarantees; tests in CI; team access.

## Examples

Plain HTTP, no SDK, TypeScript and Python, each tested end to end:

- [Telegram echo (WebSocket stream, no public URL)](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/telegram-echo)
- [Telegram AI support agent (history per conversation, "Talk to a human" button, Idempotency-Key)](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/telegram-ai-agent)
- [Webhook receiver (Flow-Signature, dedupe on event.id, reply in the answer)](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/webhook-receiver)
- [Your own Telegram bot (POST /v1/senders with a live key)](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/own-telegram-bot)

With the TypeScript SDK (`npm install @flow-engineer/messaging`):

- [Echo agent, 20 lines](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/echo)
- [Vercel AI SDK](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/vercel-ai-sdk)
- [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/openai-agents)
- [Claude Agent SDK](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/claude-agent-sdk)
- [Mastra](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/mastra)
- [LangChain.js](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/langchain)
- [Eve](https://github.com/flow-engineer/sdk/tree/main/examples/eve)
